## Validation Contract Coverage

- VAL-001: Migration 0017 creates exactly the declared objects and nothing else,
  introspected at accepted schema 17.
- VAL-002: The Obligation registration discriminator enforces both states.
- VAL-075: The 0013 and 0015 baseline diff is exactly the seven accepted hunks.
- VAL-003: The progressive fence rejects every unimplemented Phase 23 Event.
- VAL-004: `foreign_key_check` and `integrity_check` are clean after 0017 and
  after a full rebuild.
- VAL-005: The `evidence_records` rebuild preserves every prior receipt row
  **and its Artifact links** on a seeded workspace migrated in place.

Full sources, pass and fail criteria, and validator ownership are in
`project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/qa/validation-contract.md`.

## Scope

### Files To Create Or Modify

- `migrations/0013_p21_operational_kernel.up.sql` - only the accepted rows.
- `migrations/0015_p22_recovery.up.sql` - only the accepted rows.
- `migrations/0017_p23_review_judgment.up.sql`, `.down.sql` - new.
- `internal/db/` - migration loading, latest-schema expectations, tests.
- `internal/journal/project_effects.go`, `current_event_catalog.go` and tests.
- `internal/journal/current_event_columns.go` - register all ten new Phase 23
  tables in `currentEventTables` with the column domains of the 0017 DDL:
  `review_records`, `review_findings`, `finding_dispositions`,
  `judgment_concerns`, `deviations`, `decision_refs`, `human_outcomes`,
  `envelope_protected_decisions`, `requirement_refs`, and
  `requirement_issue_links` (R-14). Task 15 renames the `judgment_concerns`
  key with the table; no other task edits this map.
- `internal/export/archive_semantics_catalog.go` - mirror the nine new
  `currentEventRules` rows into `semanticEventRules` from the same
  `schema.md` section 6.2 source (R-14). Standing rule in
  `execution-scope.md` section 6: a task that changes a journal Event rule
  mirrors it here in the same task.
  In the same file and the same change, add the nine families to
  `semanticPhase22Events` at `:85` and correct that map's name to say what it
  means - families that do not exist at projection 14 (DEC-233). Mirroring the
  rules makes `found` true for the nine at **every** profile, so
  `validateEvent` (`archive_semantics.go:328`) would otherwise accept
  `review.recorded` inside a legacy projection-14 archive: the exact hole Phase
  22 added that map to close. This is provable with a crafted legacy archive and
  no Event, which is why it is task 1's and not an unfencing task's. VAL-065 is
  unaffected - the manifest check at `archive_validation.go:130` already rejects
  a cross-version archive with `schema-unsupported` before any Event is read.
- `internal/export/` - manifest projection schema and its fixtures.
- Matching in-package tests and `cmd/fid/integration/` fixtures invalidated by
  this change.
- `cmd/fid/integration/main_test.go` - stop the per-run binary-directory leak
  (test infrastructure only, no product behavior; CF-042, corrected under
  R-15). Measured cause: five tests re-execute the test binary as a child
  process, each child re-enters `runIntegrationSuite`, creates its own
  directory and rebuilds the same ~16 MB binary, and the crash-process children
  exit abnormally by design and never reach `RemoveAll`. One clean tagged run -
  exit 0, no kill, no timeout - leaked **20 directories and 306 MB** into a
  3.9 GB RAM-backed `/tmp`. At roughly 26 tagged runs this phase that is about
  7.8 GB, so `/tmp` fills around the twelfth run and the gates become
  environment-blocked rather than failing. Required change: have
  `runIntegrationSuite` publish the built binary path in an environment
  variable after a successful build, and have a process that finds that
  variable set and pointing at an existing executable reuse it - building
  nothing and removing nothing. Only the building process removes its own
  directory, exactly as today. All five re-executing call sites already spawn
  with `append(os.Environ(), ...)`, so they inherit it and need no edit; a
  variable pointing at a missing path must fall back to building. Keep the
  bounded 24-hour prune of stale `fid-integration-binary-*` directories before
  creating a directory, as the residual safety net for a parent killed mid-run;
  age is the only safe bound, because a count- or newest-based prune would
  delete a concurrent run's live binary. Record in the completion report the
  `fid-integration-binary-*` directory count and `/tmp` free space immediately
  before and after the tagged gate; a clean run must leak none. The durable
  cleanup-on-kill design stays with CF-042.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/tasks/task-1-done.md`.

### Files To Read For Context

- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/schema.md` - sections 1, 2, 3, 6, 7.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/contracts.md` - sections 1 and 2 only.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/execution-scope.md`,
  `v1-convergence-inventory.md`, `contract-coverage.md`.
- `migrations/0015_p22_recovery.up.sql` and `0016_p22_remove_escalations.up.sql`
  as the closest precedent for shape and down behavior.

### Out Of Scope

- Any domain rule, CLI leaf, Human text, or capability advertisement.
- Migration 0018 and every V1 removal.
- Deleting any fence key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Latest-schema object inventory at schema 17 equals the accepted DDL
  exactly. (VAL-001)
- [ ] Both invalid and both valid registration-discriminator inserts behave as
  accepted. (VAL-002)
- [ ] The `0013` and `0015` diff against the planning base is exactly the seven
  accepted hunks, all inside `envelope_obligations`, `work_claims`, `stops`, and
  `attention_items`; every other line is byte-identical. (VAL-075)
- [ ] Every one of the nine Phase 23 Event types is rejected by the fence with
  a byte-identical projection afterwards. (VAL-003)
- [ ] `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` and `PRAGMA integrity_check` are clean after
  0017 and after a full journal rebuild. (VAL-004)
- [ ] On a seeded schema-16 workspace whose receipt Evidence carries
  `evidence_artifact_links` rows, migrated in place through the ordinary
  catch-up path, the migration succeeds, every Evidence row is identical column
  by column with the two added columns (`review_id`, `human_outcome_id`) null
  (count corrected by DEC-267), every link row is restored with its
  exact `required_material`, and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` is empty. A
  link-free seed alone does not satisfy this criterion. (VAL-005)
- [ ] A crafted legacy archive at `ProjectionSchema` 14 carrying a
  `review.recorded` Event is rejected by `validateEvent`, and the same archive
  at the current projection schema is not rejected for that reason. (No VAL ID:
  VAL-065 correctly does not cover this - the legacy branch at
  `archive_validation.go:127-129` admits profile-14 archives by design, which is
  why `semanticPhase22Events` has to do the work. I-35, DEC-234.)
- [ ] Full required commands terminate; preserve red/green and failed-attempt
  evidence with output tokens and observed exit status.
- [ ] Every converged retained row identifies introducing commit, phase/task,
  invalidating change, and the exact command that executes it.

## Exact Commands To Run

Working directory: repository root `/home/mark/projects/fid`, or the isolated
same-task worktree root explicitly recorded by the Runner. No command is a
placeholder. Apply gofmt and goimports to edited Go files before the final gate.

After implementation, every command below is required before task close.
The tagged integration gate is mandatory from this task.

```text
gofmt -l cmd internal
golangci-lint run ./...
go test -race -timeout 30m -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
go tool cover -func=coverage.out
go test -tags integration -race -timeout 30m ./cmd/fid/integration/...
go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkRebuildWorkspace100kEvents$' -benchtime 1x ./internal/journal/
```

Two gates run for minutes and are explicitly bounded (DEC-227): the `-timeout
30m` above replaces Go's implicit 10-minute per-binary default, which the tagged
suite already approaches at 560 s. Record in the completion report the wall time
`go test` reports for `cmd/fid/integration`, `cmd/fid`, and `internal/workflow`,
so a regression is attributed to the task that caused it. Budgets: tagged
integration under 900 s and no ordinary package over 600 s (VAL-079). A breach is
a bounded speed repair owned by this task when this task's own new journeys
caused it; otherwise stop and escalate. Never record a timed-out gate as `PASS`.

No exception to the full task gate. Commands whose expected pass is non-zero:
none. Focused red/green selections never replace these commands. Report each
attempt with the command's own output token and observed termination, as
required by `AGENTS.md`. An interrupted or hung command is never `PASS`;
preserve all failed attempts and rerun the byte-identical command after an
authorized causal repair. Report lint is a Runner control after the report
commit, not a Developer gate.

- Original schema-expectation failures and original benchmark `32.500159404s` / `FAIL github.com/mbell-nzl/fid/internal/journal 35.245s` (terminated `exit_code: 1`) remain in the historical report. This session reproduced `100k-event rebuild = 33.049607193s, want <30s` (terminated `exit_code: 1`). Repeated preparation of FK-aware writes dominated the regression; scoped prepared reuse repairs it. The exact rerun passed at `23338 ms/rebuild` and the final three measurements above pass. Earlier pragma/locking experiments are not present.
- The original retained transition assertion failure (`FAIL`, terminated `exit_code: 1`) came from `0ced511b`, predating Phase 23. A deterministic regression reproduced the cached expired claim. Fresh per-clone claims/Runs repair its premise while preserving expiry behavior and expected reasons. The focused rerun and the full exact race gate pass.
- A new failure-preservation test initially failed with `no such file or directory` / `FAIL` (terminated `exit_code: 1`): its helper created directories, not the original DB. Creating and closing that DB before its snapshot repaired setup; the byte-identical focused command then passed.

Neither is counted as a passing gate. Removing repeated bootstrap setup, supported by before/after measurements and isolation tests, led to the byte-identical fresh attempt 3 above. Both script invocations terminated `exit_code: 1` and their logs are retained. - Report-lint initially printed `FAIL report-lint found 7 failure(s)` (terminated `exit_code: 7`): punctuation and explanatory prose followed the required termination suffix on seven PASS rows. Moving that prose to continuation lines repairs only report formatting. The failed output is preserved in `qa/esc-23-002-evidence/report-lint-attempt-1.log`; the exact control is rerun after committing this correction.

## Concerns, technical debt, or notes for the Tech Lead

- The canonical ledger deliberately still ends at its historical STOP. Follow `qa/resume-after-esc-23-002.md` to append the verified DEC-238 resume/recovery/resolution, then Task 1 COMPLETE. No later task was dispatched; tasks 9-11 remain held.

## Dependency-budget note

## Validation Contract Coverage

- VAL-058: Every new leaf has Human text matching the accepted obligations and
  adds no JSON member.
- VAL-059: `resume` reports real Findings plus bounded judgment sections and
  per-Obligation evaluations, and refuses to truncate silently.
- VAL-060: Human text never presents a judgment fact as deterministic proof and
  never reproduces project prose.
- VAL-073: advanced here; the new Human views follow the accepted CF-040
  guidance. The assertion itself is Human-validated at phase end.
- VAL-070, VAL-071, VAL-072: this task owns the runnable Human fixtures and
  invocation instructions for all three phase-end Human rows (R-10). The
  judgment stays with the Human; this task only makes it executable.

## Scope

### Files To Create Or Modify

- `internal/workflow/resume.go`, `resume_actions.go`.
- `cmd/fid/resume.go`, `resume_human.go`, `resume_human_guidance.go`.
- Human renderers for each Phase 23 leaf under `cmd/fid/`.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/qa/human-fixtures.md` - new; the verbatim
  Human-text fixtures the window 13-15 review checks, plus the Human-run
  checkpoints for VAL-070, VAL-071, and VAL-072 with absolute invocation
  arguments.
- `cmd/fid/integration/p23_human_fixtures_test.go` - new tagged generator,
  following the `p22_human_fixtures_test.go` precedent: it builds the seeded
  workspaces and emits a manifest with the binary digest, source commit, and the
  exact `cwd` plus argument vectors the Human runs. It must seed (a) a
  mixed-state Review with resolved, addressed, and still-blocking Findings
  (VAL-070); (b) a protected Decision blocking a guarded action, with an
  activated `human`-type Actor holding `human-outcome.record` so the Human can
  run the blocked action, record the Outcome, and rerun (VAL-071); and (c) an
  exhausted `review-cycles` budget with its Stop and Attention (VAL-072).
- Matching in-package tests and `cmd/fid/integration/` fixtures.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/tasks/task-14-done.md`.

### Files To Read For Context

- `contracts.md` section 14; `public-interface.md` sections 2 and 7.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-22/public-interface.md` section 6 and
  `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-22/qa/human-fixtures.md` for the accepted
  DEC-219 Human-guidance pattern.
- `task-13-done.md`; `execution-scope.md`; `contract-coverage.md`.

### Out Of Scope

- Trajectory economics and the full Human Validation Brief, which stay Phase 25.
- Redesign or verbosity rework of pre-existing Phase 21 and Phase 22 views.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every new leaf has a Human fixture satisfying each stated obligation and
  introducing no member absent from JSON. (VAL-058)
- [ ] Resume reports real Findings and every declared section, reproducible from
  durable state, with `result-limit-exceeded` past a bound. (VAL-059)
- [ ] No fixture claims proof for a judgment fact or embeds decision or
  requirement prose. (VAL-060)
- [ ] Every new view has labeled sections, an operation purpose line, and no
  routine narration. (VAL-058)
- [ ] `qa/human-fixtures.md` records the verbatim output used by the window
  review.
- [ ] Full required commands terminate with preserved red/green evidence.
- [ ] Every converged retained row records its provenance and executing command.

## Exact Commands To Run

Working directory: repository root `/home/mark/projects/fid`, or the isolated
same-task worktree root explicitly recorded by the Runner. No command is a
placeholder. Apply gofmt and goimports to edited Go files before the final gate.

After implementation, every command below is required before task close.
The tagged integration gate is mandatory and is never substituted.

```text
gofmt -l cmd internal
golangci-lint run ./...
go test -race -gcflags=modernc.org/...=-d=checkptr=0 -timeout 30m -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
go tool cover -func=coverage.out
go test -tags integration -race -gcflags=modernc.org/...=-d=checkptr=0 -timeout 30m ./cmd/fid/integration/...
```

Two gates run for minutes and are explicitly bounded (DEC-227): the `-timeout
30m` above replaces Go's implicit 10-minute per-binary default, which the tagged
suite already approaches at 560 s. Record in the completion report the wall time
`go test` reports for `cmd/fid/integration`, `cmd/fid`, and `internal/workflow`,
so a regression is attributed to the task that caused it. Budgets: tagged
integration under 900 s and no ordinary package over 600 s (VAL-079). A breach is
a bounded speed repair owned by this task when this task's own new journeys
caused it; otherwise stop and escalate. Never record a timed-out gate as `PASS`.

Required-command rules live in `AGENTS.md` (Commands): every required command
is reported `PASS`, or `BLOCKED` with reason; missing, silently skipped, or
narrower substituted commands are failed gates. No exception to the full task
gate. Focused red/green selections never replace these commands. Report each
attempt with the command's own output token and observed termination. An
interrupted or hung command is never `PASS`; preserve all failed attempts and
rerun the byte-identical command after an authorized causal repair. Report lint
is a Runner control after the report commit, not a Developer gate.

## Validation Contract Coverage

- VAL-004: `foreign_key_check` and `integrity_check` are clean after 0018 and
  after a full rebuild.
- VAL-061: Every removed table, index, trigger, view column, column, Event type,
  rule, and CLI leaf is absent from the latest schema and the built binary. The
  inventory must include the `requirements.last_synced_hash` column (moved here
  from VAL-053) and the two triggers 0018 drops implicitly with their tables,
  `decisions_epic_kind_guard_insert` and
  `task_completions_issue_kind_guard_insert`. Record the measured
  `issues_enriched` column list: it is identical across 0018, so the accepted
  view-column removal set is empty and that clause is satisfied vacuously.
- VAL-062: The rebuilt `issues_enriched` view and link and activity triggers
  behave exactly as accepted, and a seeded 17-to-18 probe holding both Issue and
  non-Issue `links` and `activity_log` rows proves 0018's deletes remove exactly
  the non-Issue rows.
- VAL-063: Maintenance checks over removed tables are removed and the remaining
  checks pass.
- VAL-055 (DEC-262 part): the `requirement`/`decision`-subject activity rows
  land with 0018's trigger, and the full ten-name activity-log inventory is
  recorded here as VAL-055's final outcome.

## Scope

### Files To Create Or Modify

- `migrations/0018_p23_remove_v1_judgment.up.sql`, `.down.sql` - new.
- `internal/issues/` - delete `ac_verify.go`, `concern_raise.go`,
  `concern_address.go`, `concern_list.go`, `capability_unavailable.go`, and the
  completion and verification readers in `detail.go`, `get.go`, `list.go`,
  `issue.go`, `read.go`, `ac.go`, `transition_rules.go`.
- `internal/workflow/rules.go`, `registry.go`, `workflow.go` - delete the three
  role-bound rules, their evaluators, and the roles parameter.
- `internal/maintenance/errors.go`, `warnings.go`, `operational.go`, `check.go`.
- `internal/stats/stats.go` - the dropped column only.
- `internal/journal/current_event_catalog.go`,
  `internal/journal/current_event_columns.go`,
  `internal/journal/current_event_updates.go`,
  `internal/journal/current_event_json.go`, and
  `internal/export/archive_semantics_catalog.go` - carry the
  `judgment_concerns` -> `concerns` rename through all five closed catalogs in
  this task: the two concern effect rules, the `currentEventTables` key with
  its column domains, the `validateCurrentUpdate` admission entry and any
  terminal-values guard task 8 added, the two `judgment_concerns.*_json` column
  entries, and the mirrored `semanticEventRules` rows (R-14, DEC-232). No other
  rule or table moves. The `execution-scope.md` section 6 registry inventory is
  the checklist; every row naming the old table name is renamed here.
- `internal/journal/`, `internal/db/` - latest-schema expectations and rebuild
  parity.
- `internal/export/` - projection schema 18 and its fixtures.
- `cmd/fid/issue_ac.go`, `concern.go` - delete the removed leaves.
- Matching in-package tests and `cmd/fid/integration/` fixtures, including the
  four pinned fail-closed conformance fixtures.
- `project-docs/docs/phases/phase-23/tasks/task-15-done.md`.

### Files To Read For Context

- `schema.md` sections 4, 5, 7; `contracts.md` section 15;
  `v1-convergence-inventory.md` in full.
- `migrations/0014_p21_retire_v1_authority_execution.up.sql` and
  `migrations/0016_p22_remove_escalations.up.sql` as the removal precedents.
- `task-14-done.md`; `execution-scope.md`; `contract-coverage.md`.

### Out Of Scope

- `triage_events`, the triage-status projection, `agent_runs` beyond its dropped
  column, `epic_metadata`, historical stats behavior, and old migrations.
- Capability advertisement, which is task 17.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` and `PRAGMA integrity_check` are clean after
  0018 and after a full journal rebuild. (VAL-004)
- [ ] Every inventory removal row is proven absent by a projection or
  real-process probe. (VAL-061)
- [ ] Open-Concern counts derive from generic Concerns for Issue subjects only
  and each rebuilt trigger rejects exactly its declared invalid input.
  (VAL-062)
- [ ] No maintenance check references a removed table and the command reports no
  unexpected finding. (VAL-063)
- [ ] `requirement-referenced`, `requirement-linked`, `decision-referenced`,
  and `requirement`-subject Concern/Deviation rows are written with the
  `schema.md` section 6.2 subject, and the corpus's activity log holds all ten
  added names from their producing leaves with no name outside the set.
  (VAL-055, DEC-262)
- [ ] Full required commands terminate with preserved red/green evidence.
- [ ] Every converged retained row records its provenance and executing command.

## Exact Commands To Run

Working directory: repository root `/home/mark/projects/fid`, or the isolated
same-task worktree root explicitly recorded by the Runner. No command is a
placeholder. Apply gofmt and goimports to edited Go files before the final gate.

After implementation, every command below is required before task close.
The tagged integration gate is mandatory and is never substituted.

```text
gofmt -l cmd internal
golangci-lint run ./...
go test -race -gcflags=modernc.org/...=-d=checkptr=0 -timeout 30m -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
go tool cover -func=coverage.out
go test -tags integration -race -gcflags=modernc.org/...=-d=checkptr=0 -timeout 30m ./cmd/fid/integration/...
go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkRebuildWorkspace100kEvents$' -benchtime 1x ./internal/journal/
rg -n --glob '!*_test.go' "task_completions|ac_verifications" cmd internal
rg -n --glob '!*_test.go' "requirement\.synced|last_synced_hash" cmd internal
rg -n --glob '!*_test.go' "has_completion_report|concerns_addressed" cmd internal
```

Two gates run for minutes and are explicitly bounded (DEC-227): the `-timeout
30m` above replaces Go's implicit 10-minute per-binary default, which the tagged
suite already approaches at 560 s. Record in the completion report the wall time
`go test` reports for `cmd/fid/integration`, `cmd/fid`, and `internal/workflow`,
so a regression is attributed to the task that caused it. Budgets: tagged
integration under 900 s and no ordinary package over 600 s (VAL-079). A breach is
a bounded speed repair owned by this task when this task's own new journeys
caused it; otherwise stop and escalate. Never record a timed-out gate as `PASS`.

Required-command rules live in `AGENTS.md` (Commands): every required command
is reported `PASS`, or `BLOCKED` with reason; missing, silently skipped, or
narrower substituted commands are failed gates. No exception to the full task
gate. Focused red/green selections never replace these commands. Report each
attempt with the command's own output token and observed termination. An
interrupted or hung command is never `PASS`; preserve all failed attempts and
rerun the byte-identical command after an authorized causal repair. Report lint
is a Runner control after the report commit, not a Developer gate.

List any conditional command required by this task and why:

- the named fresh-process rebuild benchmark, because this task changes the latest schema and the replay corpus.

## Expected Non-Zero Commands

These three commands prove absence, so their pass condition is a non-zero exit.
Record the real observed status; never convert it to `exit 0 (no output)`.

- `rg -n --glob '!*_test.go' "task_completions|ac_verifications" cmd internal` - expected `exit_code: 1` - no production reader or writer of the removed completion and verification tables remains.
- `rg -n --glob '!*_test.go' "requirement\.synced|last_synced_hash" cmd internal` - expected `exit_code: 1` - the removed requirement sync Event and column have no remaining production producer or consumer.
- `rg -n --glob '!*_test.go' "has_completion_report|concerns_addressed" cmd internal` - expected `exit_code: 1` - the two removed transition rules have no remaining evaluator or registration.

The `!*_test.go` exclusion is deliberate and is not a narrowed gate. Tests that
are explicitly scoped to earlier migrations retain those historical names by
design, and `migrations/` legitimately contains them in the files that create
and drop them. The authoritative absence proof is the latest-schema projection
query and the real-process leaf probe recorded under VAL-061; these searches are
supporting evidence for the production source tree only. If any search returns a
match, it is a real finding: repair the production reader or return
`RECOVERY_REQUIRED`. Never widen or narrow the declared command to make it pass.
